reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because the speaker criticizes OneCoin as an MLM-style scam and explicitly tells viewers not to invest in it. He discusses his team's planned cryptocurrency education materials, but describes them as unfinished and does not ask viewers to pay, enroll, or send financial information.

citations.quote: guys do not invest into one coin it's a bunch of bs
they're trying to make money off of you by recruiting you to join their programs

If you look at their website on their home page they sell packages education packages from one hundred and ten euros one hundred and ten euros all the way up to twenty seven thousand five hundred euros

opening.argument: The central transaction described here is not merely discussion of a coin: it is a recruitment chain tied to payment. The speaker explains that participants recruit others, collect their fees, and pass part of the money upward. He then applies that structure directly to OneCoin, saying people are recruited and charged as much as 27,000 euros. That connects the prospect of joining and recruiting with a money flow through uplines and downlines, which is characteristic of a tiered commission operation rather than ordinary commentary about cryptocurrency.

citations.quote: The way that multi-level marketing schemes work is that you recruit people and you make them pay a f.e
then you take th.hundred and you pay a piece of it to me and then i pay it to the upline
when you're trying to recruit people and you're making them pay you you know 27,000 euros for it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The warning language does not eliminate the transaction the speaker himself describes. Saying “do not invest” is a conclusion, while the underlying account still links recruitment, joining programs, and payments. The reference framing also treats the packages as merely education, even though the speaker contrasts them with a supposed coin and describes recruitment into programs. That combination supports viewing the content as evidence of a tiered solicitation, not just neutral criticism.

citations.quote: guys do not invest into one coin it's a bunch of bs
they're trying to make money off of you by recruiting you to join their programs
if you are a multi-level marketing site be clear that you are a multi-level marketing site

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These excerpts report the speaker’s allegation and explanation of how MLMs work; they do not establish that this video recruits viewers, that OneCoin actually paid commissions, or that viewers were asked to join. The speaker explicitly tells viewers not to invest and says the packages are something OneCoin allegedly sold. Describing a suspected scheme is not itself participation in a tiered commission structure.

citations.quote: guys do not invest into one coin it's a bunch of bs
we are very clear on that. We are not trying to recruit people
i hope that this video protects you and others out there from being scammed

opening.argument: Several red flags appear together: a supposed cryptocurrency is described as claiming it could overcome Bitcoin, while the associated site allegedly sells packages from 110 euros to 27,500 euros and recruits people into programs. The speaker also describes the structure as relying on uplines and downlines and says money is collected from recruited participants. Taken together, a sweeping superiority claim, high-priced packages, and recruitment-based payments make the offering look like a commission-driven scheme using cryptocurrency language to attract participation.

citations.quote: the 1Coin people they claimed that this is the second that's going to overcome Bitcoin
they sell packages education packages from one hundred and ten euros one hundred and ten euros all the way up to twenty seven thousand five hundred euros
they have an upline and downline the upline are the people who recruited you that's above you and the downline are the people that you recruited below you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense isolates the anti-investment conclusion and leaves out the warning signs that make the conclusion intelligible. The speaker does not describe an ordinary coin with incidental education; he describes a claimed Bitcoin-beating asset alongside unusually expensive packages and recruitment. Calling the video a warning does not make those specific signals disappear, and the combination is more probative than any single sentence.

citations.quote: they claimed that this is the second that's going to overcome Bitcoin
all the way up to twenty seven thousand five hundred euros
they're trying to make money off of you by recruiting you to join their programs

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The supposed red flags are presented as criticism of another entity, not as promises made by this video. The quoted superiority claim is attributed to “the 1Coin people,” and the package prices are reported as part of the speaker’s investigation. Nothing here shows that this video asks viewers to recruit anyone, buy a package, or expect commissions. Reporting suspicious conduct while advising against it is consistent with an anti-scam warning.

citations.quote: the 1Coin people they claimed that this is the second that's going to overcome Bitcoin
do not recommend that anybody that's listening to my channel recommend or even waste time looking at onecoin
if you guys have some friends or family that you don't want

opening.argument: Although the speaker presents himself as a critic, the video repeatedly centers the mechanics of joining, recruiting, and making money through cryptocurrency programs. He explains how fees move from recruits to an upline, discusses expensive packages, and contrasts OneCoin with his own cryptocurrency investment education. That framing can function as promotion of the broader opportunity model: it normalizes recruitment-based income while positioning the speaker’s channel and team as the credible alternative. The warning label therefore does not by itself prevent the content from steering viewers toward participation in related programs.

citations.quote: then you take th.hundred and you pay a piece of it to me and then i pay it to the upline
My team we are in the process of working on a cryptocurrency investment program
we are an education channel. We teach people simply how to invest and profit from the cryptocurrency boom

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the speaker’s stated warning as dispositive, but the video also gives sustained attention to recruitment mechanics, paid packages, and the speaker’s own investment education. That comparison creates a promotional contrast: OneCoin is condemned while the speaker’s channel and future program are presented as the legitimate way to learn and profit. The apparent investigation can therefore steer viewers toward the speaker’s alternative rather than operate as detached reporting.

citations.quote: My team we are in the process of working on a cryptocurrency investment program
we are an education channel. We teach people simply how to invest and profit
if you're an education site be clear that you are an education site

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The comparison is expressly defensive and distinguishes education from recruitment; it does not ask viewers to enroll or pay. The speaker says the materials are still being developed and describes his purpose as sharing mistakes and lessons. Most importantly, he tells viewers not to invest in OneCoin and says he wants to protect others. Those statements undermine the claim that the video promotes the criticized scheme or solicits participation in a substitute.

We are just, sharing our experience of the mistake that we made
i hope that this video protects you and others out there from being scammed
